text:
maya: Heads up — PR #4123 is blocked by SAST in CI. Failure looks like 'insecure-temp-file' in our test harness but I think it's a false positive. CI: https://ci.redwood/pipelines/4123/builds/7

sam: okay can you paste the snippet? most of these are test fixtures not shipping code

maya: here's the failing part from test-utils/tmpfile.go:
```go
func TempFile(t *testing.T) string {
  f, err := os.CreateTemp("", "test-")
  if err != nil {
    t.Fatal(err)
  }
  defer f.Close()
  return f.Name()
}
```

luke: yeah that matches the scanner fingerprint. Historically we suppress the rule for internal test-only helpers but need an evidence bundle and a suppression ticket.

anita: quick Q — does the scanner need KMS access to fetch suppression signatures? I got an alert that scanner-sa failed to decrypt a key when running in staging earlier.

scan-bot: scan-job-91234: SAST rule 'TEMP_FILE_CREATION' triggered on path test-utils/tmpfile.go:12
  evidence: os.CreateTemp usage
  link: https://scans.redwood/internal/scans/91234

sam: the scanner itself doesn't call KMS normally. The failure you saw was from the pre-scan hook trying to load a private rule pack stored encrypted in S3. That pre-scan sidecar runs with scanner-sa which needs kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:alias/scan-rulepack

anita: ah ok. So two things: (A) fix SA permissions for the pre-scan sidecar to avoid unrelated failures, (B) for this PR we do a temporary suppression following the triage playbook.

maya: proposed suppression workflow (short):
1) Create JIRA SEC-PR-4123 with rationale + test snippet + CI link
2) Add @sast-suppress label on the PR (auto-gated for 48h)
3) Create suppression entry in suppressions DB with evidence payload and reviewer = @luke
4) Follow up: add a unit test variant that uses t.TempDir() wrapper to satisfy future scans

luke: fine with that. I'll review the evidence quickly. For the suppression DB entry use metadata: rule_id=TEMP_FILE_CREATION, path=test-utils/tmpfile.go, reason="test fixture safe: not used in prod", expiry=30d

oncall-sre: re KMS perms, heads up we already have a scoped IAM policy for scanner pre-scan container: ScanPreHookPolicy. If scanner-sa is failing it's probably because the service account rotated and the IAM binding wasn't reattached in staging. I'll patch that and redeploy the pre-scan job in ~20m.

sam: can we avoid manual suppressions piling up? suggestion: extend the suppression review job to auto-expire test-only suppressions after 30d and add a checklist item to convert those to scanner-whitelist patterns in rulepack PRs.

luke: agree. I'll add a short RFC to the security-ops backlog: auto-expire suppressions + rulepack whitelist flow. Will ping in #eng-security when it's up.

maya: created SEC-PR-4123 and attached evidence + CI logs: https://jira.redwood/browse/SEC-PR-4123

anita: thanks — for the immediate blocker I'll approve the suppression once luke adds the DB entry and oncall-sre confirms pre-scan redeploy.

oncall-sre: pre-scan redeploy done. scanner-sa now has kms:Decrypt; re-run passed for other PRs.

scan-bot: re-run-scan-91500: passed (no new SAST issues)

luke: suppression DB entry created by me: id sup-2026-07, expiry=2026-08-26, reviewer=luke. I left a TODO in the PR to follow up with a rulepack change.

maya: great, merging now. please @here if the auto-expire flow needs follow-up. :thumbsup:

sam: small follow-up: can we add audit log tags for suppression creators so we can query who approved what? good to have when we do retrospective.

luke: yep will include audit metadata in the RFC.

maya: thanks everyone. closing thread.
